common_name: Seven Year Love Squash (Long-Storage Japanese Heirloom Squash)

planting.note: Direct sow after all frost danger has passed and soil is thoroughly warm, giving the vigorous vines plenty of room to ramble; cure harvested fruit in a warm, dry spot for a couple of weeks before moving to cool, dry long-term storage.

directions: Direct sow 1 inch deep once soil has thoroughly warmed after the last frost, spacing hills to give the sprawling vines room to run, and water deeply but infrequently to encourage a strong root system. Seven Year Love is a Japanese heirloom moschata squash, named and prized above nearly all other winter squash for its exceptional keeping ability — properly cured fruit stored in a cool, dry spot can remain sound and good to eat for many months, and the name reflects a reputation for storage life that far outlasts typical winter squash. The tan to buff, hard-shelled fruit has dense, sweet, deep orange flesh that, like other moschata types, holds its quality and flavor well even after long storage rather than turning stringy or bland. Cure fruit in a warm, dry location for one to two weeks after harvest to harden the rind and improve storage life, then keep in a cool, dry, well-ventilated space out of direct sun.
